summary: Prompt human review is supported for a sensitive goals-of-care conversation alongside, not instead of, clinical assessment. The record shows progression from breathlessness on stairs with mild ankle oedema and a 1.8 kg weight increase in May 2026 to sleeping propped up, needing pauses after a short walk, and swelling to the shins by 26 July 2026. A June renal/electrolyte abnormality was followed by apparently improved July values, so reversible congestion or another treatable contributor remains possible and should not be mistaken for proof of an irreversible trajectory. The snapshot does not document the patient's care priorities, family involvement, residence, active advance-care plan, or specialist/palliative involvement.

dataQuality.coverageSummary: Manifest coverage is technically complete for the batch input: one eligible 15-day snapshot succeeded, zero sources failed, and 36 unique resources were collected. Clinical breadth is nevertheless limited: the snapshot is dominated by diagnostic reports and GP contacts and lacks explicit residence, medication-list, admission, specialist, social-care, family/carer, and advance-care-planning records. Missing domains are unknown rather than normal or absent.
missingSources: No separate medication, hospital-admission, specialist, community-care, social-care, family/carer, or advance-care-planning source is represented in the eligible snapshot.
contradictions: The 19 June 2026 U&E reports creatinine 128 micromol/L and eGFR 48, while the 14 July 2026 U&E reports creatinine 30 micromol/L and eGFR 79; the snapshot provides no intervening treatment or explanation.

The earlier May note records comfort at rest, while the July note reports sleeping propped up and greater exertional limitation; this is best treated as temporal progression rather than a direct same-time contradiction.
